lifecycle.decision: Current primary own yield-futures product with ordinary pool deposits, upfront yield, FNFT position and maturity documentation; no retirement/shutdown evidence established.
notes: Current primary website links app and advertises ordinary issuer/purchaser pools. Application root is reachable; /frxeth HTTP500 alone is not shutdown evidence.
Related Revest infrastructure is explicitly one protocol lineage for this admission.

_activateCapital(ParamPacker(consumerOrder, producerOrder, false, pool.asset != vaultAsset, digestAmt, currentExchange, pool, adapter, poolId));\n                    \n                    consumerOrder.packetsRemaining -= digestAmt;\n                    producerOrder.packetsRemaining -= digestAmt; \n\n                    amount -= (digestAmt * pool.packetSize);\n\n \n            emit BatchInterestClaimed(poolId, fnftsByPool, recipient, interest);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Claims the interest for a given position\n     * @param fnftId the ID of the FNFT to claim interest on\n     * @param recipient where that interest should be sent\n     * @dev this function can either be called directly by the FNFT holder or through the OutputReceiver Proxy using the update method\n     */\n    function claimInterest(uint fnftId, address recipient) external override {\n        uint[][] memory fnftIds = new uint[][](1);\n        uint[] memory fnftIDi = new uint[](1);\n        fnftIDi[0] = fnftId;\n        fnftIds[0] = fnftIDi;\n        batchClaimInterest(fnftIds, recipient);\n    }\n    \n    ///\n    /// Revest OutputReceiver functions\n    /// \n\n    /**\n     * @notice Handles the withdrawal behavior for both interest- and principal-bearing FNFTs\n     * @param fnftId the ID of the FNFT being withdrawn \n     * @param tokenHolder The address to whom the principal or interest should be sent, as they owned the FNFT\n     * @param quantity How many FNFTs are being withdrawn within the series. Acceptable with nonReentrant\n                (interest,claimPerPacket) = _getWalletForFNFT(active.poolId).reclaimInterestAndResidual(\n                    pool.adapter, \n                    address(this), \n                    amountUnderlying, \n                    totalShares, \n                    residual\n                );\n            }\n\n            if(prinPackets > 0) {\n activated[fnftIdToIndex[fnftId]].sharesPerPacket = 0;\n                }\n            }\n\n            uint fee = interest * FEE / DENOM;\n            address asset = IERC4626(pool.adapter).asset();\n\n            IERC20(asset).safeTransfer(DEV_ADDRESS, fee);\n            IERC20(asset).safeTransfer(tokenHolder, interest - fee);\n            \n            emit activated[principalId] = Active(principalId, 1, 0, poolId);\n\n            fnftIdToIndex[principalId] = principalId;\n            fnftIdToIndex[interestId] = principalId;\n        }\n\n        emit  order.depositedShares = IERC4626(vaultAdapter).deposit(amount, _getAddressForPool(poolId)) * PRECISION / order.packetsRemaining;\n            require(order.depositedShares > 0, 'ER003'); \n        } Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.resonate.finance/resonate.md). # Resonate Overview of Resonate Resonate is the DeFi Yield futures protocol. Resonate splits apart the interest and principal components of a yield-bearing position. Those who hold tokens which may be deposited into yield-bearing systems can receive an instant, upfront payment on the present value of that future yield, in exchange for locking their tokens. An ideal solution for traders who want to receive guaranteed and consistent yield farming rewards for staking tokens or providing liquidity. For those who want to purchase the Yield Futures, or the rights to future yield, Resonate places them in a position where they can do so at a discount to the expected future value of the interest. For protocols wanting to reduce their burn rate, this discount can offer a better way to incentivize providing LPs. DeFi today is based around Yield-Farming, in which dozens of different protocols allow users to deposit their unused tokens in exchange for interest on those assets. In return users often receive derivative interest-bearing versions of those same assets. While those assets hold value based on their ability to be redeemed for their underlying asset, there has yet to be a protocol or liquid-asset that allows you to represent the future appreciation of that asset, until now. Let's assume that the current interest rate on Yearn.Finance for USDC is 10%. If I deposit 100 USDC into their vault and wait one year I will be able to withdraw 110 USDC. However, this requires you to have the patience of waiting one year. With Resonate, users can receive a fraction of this expected long-term yield as up-front payment, while the counterparty who pays out up-front receives the rights to all of that generated-interest. Powered by Revest-Finance's proprietary locking-mechanisms, both sides in this transaction are minted what we call a Financial-NFT (FNFT) representing their righs to claim those assets in the future. These NFT's are tradeable and liquid, even though the underlying assets they represent may not be. For example, a user holding an FNFT representing the rights to `10-USDC` of interest in 1-year may be able to such an FNFT on their favorite-marketplace for a `9-USDC`, profiting off the difference in what they paid to mint it, and the assets it represents. Revest FNFT's conform to the [ERC-1155 Multi-Token Standard](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1155)

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.resonate.finance/resonate-architecture/basic-resonate-structure.md). # Basic Resonate Structure The basic structure of Resonate and how matching occurs. Resonate is at its core, a peer-to-peer lending protocol, in which people who wish to receive an up-front payment (issuers) on their tokens (principal tokens) are matched with people that wish to pay for the interest on those tokens (purchasers). Resonate is comprised of a series of pools which users can choose to enter at will, and contain various differences on the terms of this matching. Any user can choose to create a pool with their desired parameters based on current market sentiments. When two counterparties enter each side of the pool, Resonate will automatically activate their capital. Issuer tokens are deposited into the yield-farm for long-term accumulation, while purchaser tokens go directly to the counterparty, and both are removed from the queue. Resonate then mints a custom Resonate FNFT to each participant, indicating their side of the transaction and representing the rights to retrieve their tokens in the future. Each pool contains the following parameters | Parameter | Detail | Can be Zero | | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | | Payout Asset | The Token which a purchaser will pay to the consumer up-front | No | | Vault-Address | Address of the yield-bearing vault in which the assets will be locked. This can include any DeFi protocol which returns a yield. | No | | Packet Size | The specific amount of tokens that will be locked in exchange for up-front payment (ex. 100 USDC) | No | | Pool Rate | The percentage of the packet-size that the producer will pay up-front for the yield on the packetsize (ex \~5% or 5 USDC) | No | | Additional Pool-Rate | An optional additional-rate which must be accued in interest-before withdrawal. | Yes\* | | Lockup Period | The amount of time the designed consumer-assets will be locked for before being able to be withdrawn and returned to the consumer. | Yes\* | \*Users must choose between leaving the lockup-period as zero or the additional-rate. Both cannot be zero and both cannot be non-zero simultaneously. Will be further explained in following pages. While users are allowed to create and enter pools at will, not all pools should be entered based on current market-conditions. For example, if the Aave lender rate is 10%, then purchasers are incentivized to only enter pools where the Pool-Rate <10%. While you are free to enter pools with a higher rate, that is discouraged. If interest-rates stay above 10% over the locking-period for the associated principal, then the purchaser will profit the difference in what they paid and what the accrued interest-was.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.resonate.finance/resonate-architecture/queues.md). # Queues Queueing System for Resonate Finance While Resonate is primarily a peer-to-peer matching system, there doesn't always exist a peer to be matched to. This is why Resonate uses a Queue System \[link for queues data structure]. A queue is a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) system that is used to track the order in which consumers are matched to purchasers. For each pool there exists both a consumer queue and a purchaser queue. When one side enters the pool, Resonate checks to see if a user on the other side exists, (I.E sees if a consumer is ready for the newly entered purchaser). If one already exists, then the system automatically exchanges the tokens between both users and mints the corresponding FNFTs into their wallets. However, if a counterparty does not exist for the user, they are placed into the queue until such a time comes. When a user enters a pool, they are submitting an *order*, which is either filled immediately or waits in the queue until a counterparty comes to fill it. An order can contain 1-or-more packets worth of Tokens. Let's take an example pool with packet-size 100 USDC and payout-rate 5%. This means that the purchaser will pay 5 USDC to the consumer for the interest on every multiple of 100-tokens they lock up. Consumers can **ONLY** submit token amounts that are direct multiples of the packet size, and purchasers can only submit multiples of the `(payout_rate * packetSize)`. This is referred to as the *number of packets*. **Every consumer packet must be matched with 1 producer-packet and vice-versa.** If Bob enters our metaphorical pool with `amount = 300 USDC`, where `amount % packetSize == 0` then `packets = amount / packetSize`they must wait until Alice enters the queue with `amount >= 5 USDC` and `amount % (payout_rate * packetSize) == 0.` If one sides' order is not able to completely fill the order of the counter-party, the remaining packets will remain in the queue until someone else enters to finish filling. Resonate will match packets in the most efficient way possible for every new order. For example, a newly entered Consumer order is capable of filling the orders of multiple different producers as long as they have enough remaining packets to keep filling (e.g. a 2-packet consumer order can fill 2-different single-packet producer orders). #### FNFT Minting Resonate mints FNFTs based on the most-efficient system of packet-matching. Each consumer packet matched means minted 1 FNFT-per-packet to the consumer. However, no matter how many consumer-packets a purchaser may be matched to, they will always receive 1 interest-FNFT. Example: 1. Bob Enters as a consumer with 5 packets worth of tokens 2. Alice Enters as a producer with 5 producer-packets worth of tokens 3. Bob receives all 5 producer-packets worth of tokens up-front, and 5 principal-FNFTs. Each Principal FNFT represents the right to 1 consumer-packet's worth of tokens 4. Alic receives **one** interest-FNFT which represents the rights to the interest on *all five* principal-FNFTs If filling a consumer/purchaser order requires matching with more than 1 counterparty-order, than more than one FNFT will be minted. Example: 1. Alice and Bob both enter the consumer-queue with 1 packet each. The queue length is 2 2. John enters the purchaser queue with 2-packets. 3. Bob and Alice each receive one principal-FNFT, John receives 2 interest-FNFT's, each representing the right to Alice/Bob's interest.

# Fixed-Term Pools

Pools which Relate to locking-periods of fixed-times

When you engage with Resonate you commit to locking up your tokens for some period of time. There are two ways this time-period is determined, the first being known as Fixed-Term

A Fixed-Term pool is one in which the locking-period of principal token amounts is known before entering, and is set at the moment of pool-creation. Upon creating a pool, the creator must specify whether they want the pool to be fixed-term and if so, how long the locking-term is. This can be anywhere from 1-day to 10-years. The term-begins at the moment of matching between peers in Resonate.

Time is specified in seconds using unix-timestamps as allowed by Solidity. While the FNFT's cannot be burned before the end of this locking period, interest-FNFT holders can collect their interest at any time during this locking period.

Pool creators may choose to offer more favorable payout-rates based on the length of the locking-period. Fixed-Term pools are advantageous to consumers since they always receive their principal back at the end regardless of how interest-rates may change during the locking-period for purchasers.

# Fixed-Return Pools

Pools which Relate to locking-periods of fixed-rates

While fixed-term pools are beneficial to consumers, they're not always advantagous to purchasers. If the interest-rate drops while funds are locked, the purchaser may end up with less yield than they had intended. As a result, Resonate supports what we call a *Fixed-Rate* pool. 

A fixed-rate pool is a novel locking mechanism that prevents the FNFT's from being withdrawn until a predetermined amount *of tokens* has been accrued in interest. Fixed-Rate pools are when the *additional-rate* variable is non-zero at pool-creation. 

Example: A fixed-rate pool has packet-size 100 USDC, Pool-Rate 5%, and Additional-Rate 1%. 

The purchaser will pay out `5 USDC = 100` USDC `* .05` up front to the consumer. Until the (`poolRate + additionalRate)* packetSize` amount of interest has been accrued, the principal FNFT cannot be withdrawn.

`(0.05 + 0.01) * 100 = 6 USDC.` **Until 6 USDC has been accrued in interest, the principal amount cannot be recovered**. While the time-until-unlock is predictable based on current market-APY, it cannot be predicted with certainty, which creates an uncertain environment for consumers. However, it also creates a very low-risk vehicle for purchasers, since over a long-enough period of time the purchaser will always recover their initial investment so long as `APY > 0.` However, since this presents new uncertainty for consumers, purchasers may be willing to offer higher-payout rates in exchange for the uncertainty of the lockup-period.

\*The amount of interest that must be accrued is measured based on the vault-asset, not the payout in the event that they are different. For example, even if you pay out USDC in exchange for interest in WETH, your interest is measured in WETH, relative to the rate and packet size in WETH, **NOT USDC**, for your protection.

$$
f(interest) \ge (poolRate + additionalRate)\*packetSize
$$
